page.layout: One page of running text, with two medallion illustrations above it. The left medallion carries the legend "PA TRO." and "CORIOLANVS"; the right carries "VETVRIA CORIO" and "MAT.". Below them: first entry (C. M. CORIOLANVS) and second entry (VETVRIA), both in one column. No margin notes, no footnotes.

main_text.l: PA TRO.
CORIOLANVS
VETVRIA CORIO
MAT.
C. M. CORIOLANVS
Patricius Romanus ab Roma-
nis exactus est, quòd Consulatum arroganter ambiret, & Tri-
bunis Plebis aduersaretur, ac proinde suspectus esse populo ob
nimium factum ac potentiam.quare cum iam ante pro Roma-
nis pugnans,Coriolos vrbem,Volscorum ciuitatem,vnde Co-
riolanus dictus est,expugnasset, ad ipsos Volscos contendit
iratus, à quibus auxilia contra Romanos accepit anno mundi
3 4 7 5. ante Christum natum 4 8 7. Romanos saepe vicit: vsque
ad quintum miliarium vrbis accessit, expugnaturus etiam pa-
triam suam(legatis qui pacem petebat repudiatis) nisi ad eum
mater Veturia & vxor Volumnia, ex vrbe venissent: quarum
precibus remouit exercitum, quem submouere armis Roma
non poterat.Vide Titum Liuium lib.2.& Eutro. lib.1.Foeminae
item preces ac lachrymae vxoris Meleagri, ad arma pro patriae
tutela capessenda Meleagrum compulerunt.Ouid.epi.3.
VETVRIA
C.M. Coriolani mater fuit, ad quam adie-
runt matronae Romanae, quae in discrimine patriae periuicerunt[?]
vt Veturia magno natu mulier, & Volumnia Coriolani vxor,
duos paruulos ex Coriolano ferentes secum,in castra hostium
irent:& quam armis viri defendere vrbem non possent,mulie-
res precibus lachrymisque defenderent: quod praestiterunt.
nam fractus precibus ac fletibus matris Veturiae ac vxoris Vo-
lumniae Coriolanus,castra retro ab vrbe mouit.Titus Liuius li.
2.Dion.Halic.lib.7.& 8. Statuit Senatus vt foemineum extrue-
retur templum Diuae Fortunae, vbi foeminae singulis annis, ea-
dem qua liberata fuerat vrbs die, sacra peragerent: idque in
foeminarum honorem, ac huius facti, & velut miraculi, moni-
mentum perpetuum.

page.notes: The two entry headings "C. M. CORIOLANVS" and "VETVRIA" stand run-in in the print, at the start of their paragraphs; they are set here on their own line. "periuicerunt" is doubtful (small, slightly blurred type). The line "mater" in the first paragraph is printed as "matet" in the scan's ink; read as "mater". Numbers "3475" and "487" are printed with spaces between the digits and are copied so. The medallion legends are part of the illustrations and are transcribed as lines.
